items.prompt: Black to move. The light-squared bishop is already outside the pawn chain on f5. Which pawn move now opens the diagonal for the f8 bishop and supports the centre?

claims.statement: f5 holds the black bishop.
e7 holds the black pawn.
After ...e6 the bishop on f8 attacks along the diagonal through e7, d6, c5 and b4.
At depth 16 e6, Nbd7, Bg6 and h6 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Look at the pawn on e7. It stands in front of the f8 bishop.
The move you want moves the pawn in front of the bishop and also guards a central square.
items.explain: ...e6 opens the diagonal for the f8 bishop (b4, c5 and d6 are now reachable) and the pawn guards d5 and f5. It is only comfortable because the c8 bishop is already outside the chain. At depth 16 e6 is the engine's first choice; Nbd7, Bg6 and h6 are also within 0.4 pawn, so e6 is a sound move here, not the only one.

items.prompt: White to move. Black took the pawn on c4 earlier, and White's e-pawn has just opened the diagonal of the f1 bishop. Which move regains the pawn?

claims.statement: c4 holds the black pawn.
The bishop on f1 attacks c4.
After Bxc4 the bishop on c4 attacks b5 and d5.
At depth 16 Bxc4 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which black pawn left its square earlier in the opening?
Which white piece already attacks that pawn?
The bishop on f1 takes the pawn on c4.
items.explain: Bxc4 regains the pawn with the bishop: the e3 pawn opened the f1 bishop's diagonal, so the bishop attacks c4. At depth 16 it is the engine's first choice.
